A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Visual Haystacks benchmark and MIRAGE framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. Rotated tables are readable, and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original VHs evaluations, MIRAGE benchmark results, retrieval/runtime comparisons, and compression ablations in Figures 2–6, Tables 1–2, and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds MIRAGE evaluations on MME and SEED-Bench, qualitative failure cases, and a multi-needle question-category analysis.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the frozen CLIP encoder, 32-query Q-Former, relevance retriever, Llama-v3.1 backbone, losses, and two-stage training. The new description of MIRAGE as an end-to-end single-model architecture clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds MME and SEED-Bench evaluations in Table 1, modestly broadening conventional single-image QA coverage. The training datasets, VHs tasks, RetVQA, and previous single-image benchmarks remain. The new multi-needle breakdown analyzes existing question types rather than introducing another task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-4o and Gemini v1.5 Pro to the reported POPE comparison, replacing their v2 dashes with 87.2 and 88.2. v3 identifies single-image baseline scores as externally sourced. The comparator sets in the retained VHs and compression experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C.4 introduces category-conditioned evaluation: accuracy across haystack sizes is reported separately for ANY-Yes/ALL-No and ANY-No/ALL-Yes questions, alongside aggregate and single-needle results. The existing VHs sample-selection rules, zero-shot setting, model configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure C.2 examines two GPT-4o/Gemini failure cases involving small or non-salient objects. Appendix C.4 and Figure C.3 investigate why multi-needle accuracy can exceed single-needle accuracy. The compression ablation is retained from v2 Table 2 as v3 Table C.2, not newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions describe bootstrapped averages with standard-deviation error bars. The uncertainty values in v2 Tables C.1–C.2 match v3 Tables C.3–C.4. No new run counts, seed disclosures, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 newly reports MIRAGE scores of 1437.9 on MME and 59.0 on SEED, together with additional baseline entries. Figures C.2–C.3 add qualitative outcomes and question-category performance curves. Previously reported VHs, RetVQA, single-image QA, and compression-ablation values are retained.

T1.justification: The image-encoding and relevance formulation in Equation 1 is unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added. The ANY/ALL discussion provides a conceptual interpretation of empirical difficulty.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Section 7 retain the principal benchmark, scalability, and performance claims. However, the new Section 5 conclusion claims faster runtimes than CLIP. This strengthens the efficiency claim beyond v2 and conflicts with the retained Figure 6 and text stating that CLIP is faster.

C2.justification: v3 explains that some multi-needle questions can be answered using one suitable image, whereas others require all relevant images, qualifying their relative difficulty. Section 5 adds a token-compression explanation for selected single-image performance deficits and a fairness argument for single-model comparisons. Existing COCO scope, bias, and generalization limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix A provides separate MIRAGE and VHs repository addresses, stated licenses, and LLaVA/POPE code provenance; v2 already advertised availability through the project page. Table 1 newly identifies the sources of single-image baseline scores. These are documentation additions, not evidence of changed training or newly available resources.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds comparisons with CompBench, MANTIS, and MUIRBench, emphasizing VHs's scale and diagnostic focus, and adds an xT citation. MME and SEED-Bench references accompany the expanded evaluation. The established relationship to retrieval-based QA and long-context models remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized rewrites in Sections 4–6, adds a results-summary paragraph and code-release appendix, and reorganizes appendix subsections. The compression discussion moves out of the main text. The overall narrative remains stable, while headers change from under review to ICLR 2025 publication.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains MME and SEED columns and changes row ordering. The compression table moves to Appendix C, and new Figures C.2–C.3 display failure cases and subgroup curves. Existing figures are retained, with limited resizing, caption edits, and appendix reflow.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's aggregate multi-needle results, v3's category breakdown gives a more informative account of retrieval and integration difficulty. Added benchmark results, baseline-source disclosure, and explicit code-access information also improve assessment and reproducibility. These are incremental gains. A countervailing defect is the new Section 5 runtime claim contradicting Figure 6; it limits, but does not outweigh, the additions' overall value.
